# Erpsept26

Source: https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/implprem/ERPSept26.xlsx

Sheets: Impl premium calculator, Buyback & Dividend computation, Expected growth rate, Implied ERP- Annual since 1960, Implied ERP (Monthly from 9-08), Historical ERP, S&P 500 Monthly Data (Cap IQ), T.Bond vs Nominal growth, Answers

## Impl premium calculator

| Implied Risk Premium Calculator | May 2025 Rating effect: On May 16, 2025, Moody's, the lone holdout among the ratings agencies, downgraded the United States from Aaa to Aa1, thus raising questions about whether the US 10-year treasury rate is really a riskfree rate. Netting out the default spread for an Aa1 rated sovereign from the US treasury rate will yield a more consistent riskfree rate in US dollars and a higher equity risk premium. While I will report my conventional measure of the ERP, with the US treasury rate as the riskfree rate, to allow for comparison with time series data, I will also report a US ERP with the adjusted riskfree rate. |
|---|---|
| Inputs |  |
| Estimation month (start of) | September |
| Base Year Earnings for the Index | Estimated |
| Enter current level of index | 7686.14 |
| What cash yield (dividends & buybacks) do you want to use as your base number? | C |
| Cash yield on index (Calculated number but you can override it) | 0.026258457676052675 |
| What expected growth rate do you want to use for the next 5 years? | TD |
| Expected growth rate in earnings for the next 5 years = | 0.13986308813275117 |
| Enter current 10-year US treasury rate rate  = | 0.0475 |
| If you want to compute an intrinsic value for index, what ERP would you like to use? | ERP10 |
| Default spread for Aa1 rating (US sovereign rating) | 0.0022 |
| ERP used to compute fair value of index (you can override this number) = | 0.0425 |
| Do you want to change the growth rate in the long term? | No |
| If yes, enter the expected growth rate to use after year 5  | 0.03 |
| Do you want to adjust the payout ratio to sustainable levels in year 5? | No |
| Here is how it works |  |
| For the intrinsic value of the index, I start with your base cash flow choice (from B5) and grow these cash flows at  |  |
| the expected growth rate (from B7) for 5 years. After year 5, I use the expected growth rate in the long term (B12) |  |
| as the perpetual growth rate. The discount rate that I use is the sum of the risk free rate (B9) and your ERP choice (B11).  |  |
| If you choose to adjust your payout ratio, I estimate the payout ratio given average ROE over last 10 years. Payout = 1 - g/ ROE |  |
| For the implied ERP, you will have to use the goal seek function in Excel. (See picture to the right) |  |
| 1. In the set cell box, enter B54 |  |
| 2.  In "To value" box, enter the current level of the index |  |
| 3. In "By changing cell" enter C45 |  |
| 4. Click on OK and the answer should show up in C45 |  |
